sources.summary: BuzzFeed News feature (12 Jan 2018), 'The Plight Of Trans Women In Prison': transgender women incarcerated in France on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal grey area and are punished for far more than their alleged crimes - first-person accounts of placement in an all-male facility (a three-day stay in Lille's men's prison in 2014, with detainee and staff hostility; an Argentinian trans woman's story of incarceration); Article D248 of the criminal procedure code assigns detainees by the sex on their ID; the controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty says transgender detainees are the group that 'suffers the most' in prison; also covers the well-publicised case of a US trans woman detained in poor conditions after a 2016 Paris protest case.

Opinion of 25 May 2021 of the Contrôleur général des lieux de privation de liberté (CGLPL), unofficial English translation: official inspectorate opinion on the treatment of transgender persons in ALL places of deprivation of liberty; built on about forty referrals received since 2010, interviews with trans associations and European experts, and five on-site inspections (Fleury-Mérogis men's and women's prisons, Caen, Saint-Martin-de-Ré, Toulouse-Seysses and the Toulouse central police station - eight trans women and one trans man interviewed); finds persistent serious violations of fundamental rights of trans detainees, isolation and overcrowding risks; recommends that the 2016 depathologising law (no more surgery requirement for civil-status change) be translated into prison regulations; explicitly extends to intersex and non-binary people.

Anti-Torture organisation news blog (interview extract with the French national preventive mechanism on its 25 May 2021 Opinion): trans persons deprived of liberty face the constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; the 2010 Opinion was insufficient given no improvement in places of detention; the new Opinion followed five dedicated inspection visits across regions and institution types; findings include no public data on trans detainees, no staff training, few national guidelines, and the 2016 depathologisation law not applied to places of detention.

localsOnly: The placement of trans detainees and prison conditions - the subject of all three sources here - affect residents who enter the justice system; a visitor is exposed only if arrested, and the sources document no region-specific detention pattern.
